answer: Convergent Answer Seeding. Each identity must submit a unique, time-stamped solution to a seeded challenge derived from live system state, and reuse of any prior answer voids it. At the nadir of the registration round, the seed rotates, forcing fresh work per identity. Entering the tundra of low-activity epochs, seeds grow sparser, raising per-answer compute cost. The zenith of attacker throughput is capped because fabricating identities requires separately solving each rotating challenge, paying full compute per identity rather than one shared answer.
